children.text: AXA Indonesia | Step 5 Loss Ratio & Profitability Review
Case study portfolio review | Policy-level aggregation of premium and claim data
Portfolio remains profitable in nominal underwriting terms, but profitability is uneven and concentrated in a few loss-making pockets.
Net loss ratio at portfolio level is 58.5%, while segment-level stress appears in COB 4, Branch K, Channel B, and Product0221.
1. Channel D is the strongest scaled segment with 17.60% net loss ratio and IDR 411.4B net underwriting result.
2. COB 3 is the best-performing class with 6.03% net loss ratio, although the policy base is smaller than major classes.
3. Reinsurance provides claim relief in nominal terms, but lower net premium means net loss ratio can still exceed gross loss ratio.
1. COB 4 is loss-making at 106.55% net loss ratio with -IDR 91.7B net underwriting result.
2. Branch K and Channel B are the two largest loss pockets, both above 100% net loss ratio.
3. Product0221 is the most material loss-making product in the filtered ranking at 120.59% net loss ratio.
